problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-8\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

feedback.problem:
Given that the expression $4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the **exact** value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=\operatorname{arctan}⁡($ 
{{field-1}} $)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
4\operatorname{sin}⁡x-9\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=9\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{9}{4} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{9}{4} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{9}{4}).\end{aligned}
$$
